tutorial.title: Boilerplate code
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about the html, body, head, title tag, and much more!

lessons.title: Element
lessons.interactiveContent:
An element is what we call the opening tag, closing tag, and code in between.

Which one of these is an element?

<button>Hello, World!</button><button><h1></p>

<button>Hello, World!</button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For elements like button, the opening tag, closing tag, and any content between them form the whole element.

You remove Hello, World! from <button>Hello, World!</button>. What remains?

A button element with no labelAn opening button tag with no closing tagThe label as plain text with no tagsNo element, because an element must have text

A button element with no label.

lessons.title: Code a heading element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an h1 element that displays My Online Store.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by My Online Store, and finally </h1>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create the largest heading that displays My Online Store.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by My Online Store, and finally </h1>.

lessons.title: HTML element
lessons.interactiveContent:
To create a webpage, you'll need an opening and closing HTML tag. Which one of these options will create an empty HTML webpage?

<html> </html><button> </button><p> </p><h1> </h1>

<html> </html>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To create a webpage, you need an opening and closing html tag.

You have written <html>. Which tag completes the matching pair for an empty webpage?

</html><html></p></h1>

Make sure to pick </html>.

lessons.title: Code an HTML element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a webpage by coding an html element.

Remember we can create an html element by coding <html> and </html>.

Make sure to pick <html>, followed by </html>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create an empty webpage with matching opening and closing html tags, in that order.

Make sure to pick <html>, followed by </html>.

lessons.title: HTML and body in depth
lessons.interactiveContent:
The html and body elements form the structure of a webpage. We place elements we want to display inside of the body.

Later, we'll learn about other elements that go inside of <html> </html> to give webpages style and make them interactive.

Make sure to pick <body>, followed by </body>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inside html, add the element that holds visible page content.

Make sure to pick <body>, followed by </body>.

lessons.title: Body element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which one of these codes defines the body of a webpage?

<body> </body><html> </html><h1> </h1><p> </p>

<body> </body>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inside html, the body element contains the content you want to display.

You put a heading after </body>. Where should you move it so it is inside the body element?

Before </body>, between the body tags.Before <html>, outside the webpage.After </html>, outside the webpage.Inside the <body> opening tag.

Before </body>, between the body tags.

lessons.title: Code the body element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the body element for this webpage.

Make sure to pick < followed by body and then >, </, body, >.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Code the body element for this webpage.

Inside html, add an opening body tag followed by its matching closing tag.

Make sure to pick <, followed by body, >, </, body, and finally >.

lessons.title: Code a heading
lessons.interactiveContent:
We must place contents, such as headings, inside the body tags. Display a heading on the webpage.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by Top Stories, and finally </h1>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inside the body, display the largest heading with the text Top Stories.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by Top Stories, and finally </h1>.

lessons.title: Code a button
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the opening tag to display a button on the webpage.

Make sure to type <button>.

lessons.title: Code a paragraph
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display a paragraph underneath the heading on the webpage.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by I love to code, and finally </p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Under the heading, use matching tags to display a paragraph that says I love to code.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by I love to code, and finally </p>.

lessons.title: Code two elements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the larger heading on top of the smaller heading.

Make sure to pick <h1>Online Store</h1>, followed by <h6>Shoes</h6>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inside the body, put Online Store in the largest heading above Shoes in the smallest heading.

Use matching opening and closing tags for each heading.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by Online Store, </h1>, <h6>, Shoes, and finally </h6>.

lessons.title: Head element
lessons.interactiveContent:
The head HTML element, <head></head>, is a container for information about a webpage, like its title. It goes before the body tag.

Make sure to pick <head>, followed by </head>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The head element holds information about a webpage, like its title. It goes before the body.

Add matching opening and closing head tags before the body, in that order.

Make sure to pick <head>, followed by </head>.

lessons.title: Viewing a title
lessons.interactiveContent:
The title of a webpage appears in the tab or window of the web browser.

In the tabs below, there are two webpage titles: My webpage and Google.

lessons.title: Title
lessons.interactiveContent:
To give a webpage a title, we add <title> and </title> inside the head tags.

Note that the title is not visible but it provides information to the browser.

Make sure to pick <title>, followed by </title>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Put title tags inside head to give the browser a title. It appears in the browser tab, not the page body.

Wrap My webpage in matching opening and closing title tags.

Make sure to pick <title>, followed by My webpage, and finally </title>.

lessons.title: Doctype
lessons.interactiveContent:
The doctype tells the web browser what version of HTML we're using. Without it, the browser might not display the page correctly.

Since we're using the latest version, we use <!doctype html>.

Make sure to pick <!doctype html>.

lessons.title: Using doctype
lessons.interactiveContent:
The doctype looks like an empty doctype tag with an empty html attribute: <!doctype html>.

Attributes provide additional information to tags. You'll learn more about them in later chapters. For now, put together the doctype.

Make sure to pick < followed by !doctype and then html, >.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The doctype looks like an empty tag with extra information: <!doctype html>.

Put together the exact latest HTML doctype before the html element.

Make sure to pick <, followed by !doctype, html, and finally >.

lessons.title: *Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the head tag for?

It's a container for information about a webpageIt makes important text like headlines stand outIt tells the web browser which version of HTML a webpage usesIt defines the title for a webpage

It's a container for information about a webpage.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A browser needs page information that is not visible content. What is the head element for?

It's a container for information about a webpageIt makes important text like headlines stand outIt tells the web browser which HTML version to useIt displays the main heading on the page

It's a container for information about a webpage.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can we define a webpage's title so that it appears in the tab or window of the web browser?

With the title tags, <title> and </title>With headline tags like <h1> and </h1>

With the title tags, <title> and </title>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which tags set the text for the browser tab or window, not a visible page heading?

The <title> and </title> tagsThe <h1> and </h1> tagsA <meta> tag in the page head

The <title> and </title> tags.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the doctype, <!doctype html>, do?

It tells the web browser which version of HTML a webpage usesIt defines the title for a webpage

It tells the web browser which version of HTML a webpage uses.
lessons.hardModeContent:
At the top of a page, what does <!doctype html> tell the browser?

Which version of HTML the webpage usesWhat title to show in the browser tabWhich character encoding the page uses

Which version of HTML the webpage uses.

lessons.title: Question 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when there's no doctype in a webpage?

The web browser has to guess the HTML versionThe web browser will quit

The web browser has to guess the HTML version.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What happens if a webpage leaves out the doctype?

The web browser has to guess the HTML versionThe body content stops showingThe browser treats the HTML file as plain text

The web browser has to guess the HTML version.

lessons.title: Example 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the correct opening tag.

Make sure to pick <, followed by title, and finally >.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the opening title tag before My page.

Make sure to pick <, followed by title, and finally >.

lessons.title: Example 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Give this movie rating webpage a title to have the web browser tab or window display Ripe Tomatoes.

Make sure to pick <title>, followed by Ripe Tomatoes, and finally </title>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Give the movie rating webpage the browser title Ripe Tomatoes.

Make sure to pick <title>, followed by Ripe Tomatoes, and finally </title>.

lessons.title: Example 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make sure the web browser knows what version of HTML to use for this cryptocurrency website.

Make sure to pick <!doctype html>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Tell the browser this cryptocurrency page uses the latest HTML version.

Make sure to pick <, followed by !doctype, html, and finally >.

lessons.title: Code 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's create a new webpage. Add the doctype , html, and body tags. Then, add some text inside the body tags.

Make sure to pick <!doctype html> followed by <html> and then <body>, It's all about conformity., </body>, </html>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Start with the doctype, then open the html element.

Inside it, wrap It's all about conformity. in matching body tags. Close html last.

Make sure to pick <!doctype html>, followed by <html>, <body>, It's all about conformity., </body>, and finally </html>.
